entries.summary: Bearish elevated-downside path persists. Reuters' 11:23 EST Nasdaq -1.74%, SOX about -6%, and AMD about -10% remain the latest explicitly time-anchored cross-market observations. Reuters also reports Nasdaq declining issues outnumbering advancers 2.03:1 and 258 new 52-week lows against 22 highs. These reinforce the already identified semiconductor-led rout, not a distinct fresh regime change.
bullish: October PPI +0.3% month on month versus +0.4% forecast offers limited inflation relief; 83.6% of S&P 500 reporters beat estimates according to Reuters/LSEG.
Apple and Meta were modestly positive at Reuters' late-morning checkpoint, and Cerebras rose on revenue guidance and a Microsoft customer announcement; isolated resilience is not broad confirmation.
bearish: Reuters reported Nasdaq -1.74% at 11:23 EST while SOX was approximately -6%, implying severe semiconductor underperformance.
Reuters reported AMD about -10%, AVGO about -7%, and Nvidia -4.3%, indicating selling beyond one issuer.
Nasdaq declining issues exceeded advancers 2.03:1 and 258 new 52-week lows versus 22 highs in Reuters' intraday coverage.
October PPI 6.5% year over year and elevated previously observed Treasury yields keep valuation risk high.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday's technology drawdown remains concentrated in semiconductors. Reuters recorded Nasdaq down 1.74% and S&P 500 down 1.01% at 11:23 EST, while its late-morning coverage described SOX falling roughly 6%, AMD roughly 10%, Broadcom roughly 7% and Nvidia 4.3%. The timestamps for individual semiconductor quotes are not fully synchronized with the index print. This is intraday evidence, not a final close.
editorial.whatChanged: The newly checked Reuters report adds breadth evidence: Nasdaq decliners outnumber advancers 2.03 to 1, with 258 new 52-week lows versus 22 highs. This supports a broader risk-off interpretation beyond the semiconductor leadership failure. However, the severe SOX drawdown and bearish path were already established in the previous assessment; no distinct new material change is confirmed. The curated Open Watch feed was refreshed at 2026-11-13T18:24:41+00:00 and has 163 events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Broadly negative participation reinforces the bearish market response to AI leadership uncertainty, while softer monthly producer inflation has not sustained the initial rally. Inflation remains uncomfortable at 6.5% annual PPI. A prior 10-year Treasury yield of 5.127% and 2-year yield of 4.836% imply a +29.1-basis-point curve spread; these are stale and cannot be used to claim synchronized bond confirmation. Reported AI earnings and foundry capacity developments are fundamental catalysts, not verified isolated price drivers.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13 faces closing risk as chip weakness and negative breadth persist. Monday November 16 is the key continuation-versus-oversold-rebound test, particularly whether SOX stabilizes relative to QQQ. Tuesday November 17 may remain volatile around AI capital-allocation concerns, rate expectations and issuer events. Bearish elevated downside remains the base case, but a sharp tactical rebound is plausible after unusually large sector declines.
editorial.bullCase: Softer-than-forecast monthly PPI, generally strong earnings beats, and pockets of megacap resilience can support a rebound if broad market breadth turns positive and SOX begins outperforming QQQ. A recovery should be judged by matched session observations and sustained follow-through, not isolated premarket or delayed quotes.
editorial.bearCase: Severe semiconductor losses combined with 2.03 decliners per advancer and 258 Nasdaq new lows indicate risk reduction extending beyond one name. A weak Friday close followed by a Monday break below Friday lows would strengthen continuation risk. Elevated prior Treasury yields and oil remain potential valuation/inflation pressures but require refreshed synchronized checks.
